name: cmd
description: Execute a Windows cmd.exe command line and stream its stdout. Hard cap 10 minutes per call; default 60s. Use this for classic cmd-style work: dir listings, copy/move, ping, ipconfig, path/registry checks, running .bat/.cmd scripts, etc. The command is written to a temp .bat file and run via `cmd.exe /d /c <bat>` so cmd's quoting rules don't apply — embedded quotes, &, |, ^, % are interpreted exactly as written. Cancellation / timeout both kill the running cmd process — there is no orphan child after the call returns.

command.description: The exact command line to run in cmd.exe. Written verbatim to a temp .bat and executed with `cmd.exe /d /c <bat>` (prefixed with `@echo off`). Use classic cmd syntax: `dir /b`, `ping -n 2 127.0.0.1`, `echo %PATH%`, `type file.txt`. Cannot be empty.

timeout.description: Maximum wall-clock seconds to wait for the command to finish. Required. Default 60, hard cap 600. The cmd process is killed if this elapses before the command returns.
